A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Visual Forager research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original human psychophysics results from 15 participants and 750 trials, alongside VF evaluations, baseline comparisons and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds sensitivity experiments, scanpath comparisons, external-baseline evaluations and a qualitative example.

M1.justification: VF retains the same feature/value modulation, eccentricity-dependent VGG16, transformer actor-critic, two-stage PPO training and inhibition-of-return mechanisms. Additional pooling and GAE/TD(lambda) explanations document the existing procedure; the PDFs do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 2,400-item source pool, human foraging task, two in-domain conditions and five OOD conditions. The added analyses and external comparisons use retained task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds four evaluated external comparators: IVSN, IVSN-NN, pretrained GazeFormer and GazeFormer fine-tuned on in-domain data. Table S6 compares them with VF on EqValUnPre, UValues, UItemNum and USetSize, substantially extending the original comparison set.

E3.justification: v3 adds ScanMatch and Fixation Edit Distance evaluation with within-subject and between-subject controls, plus pooling-scale and blank-area-penalty sweeps. These extend the evaluation protocol; the original participant count, trial limits, reward metrics and VF training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses examine pooling-scale sensitivity, intrinsic-penalty sensitivity, human–model scanpath similarity and an illustrative comparison of fixation/click sequences. The original component ablations are retained, moving from Section 5.5/Table 1 to Section S3.1/Table S3.

E5.justification: Existing error bars and t-test reporting are retained. The added tables provide point estimates without new seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or specified significance tests; the penalty study's 'no significant effect' statement supplies no statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Original headline VF scores remain 72.6%, 67.1% and 81.6%. New Tables S1 and S4–S6 add substantial results: VF's ScanMatch is 0.2474 versus chance's 0.1596, and pooling scale beta=4 yields 2.95% reward. External comparisons introduce an exception to blanket superiority: IVSN scores 77.76% on USetSize versus VF's 72.34%.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, MDP definitions, PPO objective, DQN update and inhibition-decay expression remain unchanged. Added implementation explanations and empirical metrics introduce no new theorem, proof or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and four stated contributions retain the same claims about reward-seeking behavior, VF's human-behavior approximation, baseline superiority and OOD generalization. Additional evidence and discussion qualifications do not redefine the central contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges that VF cannot model fixation duration and that its scanpath similarity falls below human-to-human similarity. It also qualifies comparisons with non-foveated baselines, explains the controlled grid-world setting and distinguishes human stimulus novelty from AI OOD generalization. Earlier limitations remain.

D1.justification: v1 promises future release; v3 supplies a repository link and states that data, code and models are available. Sections S1.4 and S2.1 additionally disclose the 30-pixels-per-degree conversion and GAE/TD(lambda) estimation choices. Hardware, training budgets and PPO hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for OAT, ScanMatch, dynamic programming and Monte Carlo sampling, while removing MEDIRL. OAT joins the related-work discussion of human-data-dependent scanpath models; the broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization are retained. v3 moves the original ablation section into the appendix, adds focused explanations and appendix subsections, updates author information and adds acknowledgements. There is no extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: Four new result tables, S1 and S4–S6, and the human/model scanpath Figure S6 substantially expand the displayed evidence. Existing figure content is preserved; the original ablation table moves to S3, the PPO table becomes S2, and figures and the title block are reflowed or resized.

improvement.justification: External comparisons, direct scanpath measurements with human controls, sensitivity analyses and added reproducibility information make VF's strengths and limitations easier to assess. The gains are limited by unresolved interpretation problems: Table S6 contradicts blanket superiority on USetSize, and the penalty study claims no significant effect without reporting uncertainty or a test.
